key_insight: CP-Agent uses a harness-engineered LLM agent to autonomously run end-to-end crystal plasticity workflows from natural-language instructions while keeping the reasoning trace visible and auditable.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce manual setup and parameter-calibration burden in constitutive modeling studies, making systematic CP simulations and inverse identification more practical for researchers.
method: ReAct-based agent decides tool sequence and workflow steps from the task description.
Typed tools, dispatcher, and safety-bounded loop encode domain knowledge in the harness rather than hard-coded control logic.
Numerical optimization is delegated to established solvers while the agent manages orchestration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports four case studies—316L calibration, copper validation and texture recovery, and Mg-Zn-Ca rolling texture evolution—where the agent inferred correct execution sequences and produced physically interpretable results across repeated runs.
watch_item: Performance depends on well-designed tool schemas and bounded iteration logic, so reliability may drop if the toolset, prompts, or domain assumptions are incomplete.
paper_title: CP-Agent: A Harness-Engineered Agent for Crystal Plasticity Simulation Workflows
